newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia priority sectors will pay less for loans.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia priority sectors will pay less for loans.

text.p: Interest rates on loans to priority sectors of the Tunisian economy such as agriculture are expected to drop by more than one percentage point, banking sources said on Tuesday.

The Central Bank of Tunisia last month cut by one percentage point the monetary market (interbank) rate to 7.8125 percent, and later told the commercial banks they were free to set their own lending rates.

The cut was immediately passed on for lending to non-priority sectors but it remained unclear how this would apply for rates on loans to priority sectors such as agriculture, export financing, handicrafts, and small- and medium-enterprises.

Central Bank officials said that if the banks do not widen their margins when passing on the cut they expect rates for priority sectors to be cut by 0.875 to 1.625 percentage points for short-term credits and by 1.375 to 2.625 percentage points for medium-term credits.
"We don't expect the banks will raise their commission margin," one official said.

Before the monetary market rate cut, priority sector rates were between 10 and 10.25 percent for short-term credits and 10 to 11 percent for medium-term credits. Commercial banks were obliged to reserve 10 percent of their resources for loans to priority sectors.
"It is a good news the BCT has eliminated mandatory financing, and we will continue to have cheaper refinancing prices for loans to priority sectors," a banker told Reuters.
But he added that this refinancing would be only through the monetary market, especially the central bank's tender (appel d'offres) rate which is lower by nearly one point than the money market rate.

In its note last week to the commercial banks, the central bank had said that the liberalisation has "resulted in eliminating the rediscount procedure to the central bank and the chanelling of any refinancing to the monetary market."

Bankers said the recourse by banks to the rediscount rates or subsidised rates has been declining for some years and that subisidised loans fell to 4.9 million dinars in 1995, from 38.6 million dinars in 1989. ($=1.0 dinar) --Tunis newsroom, 2161-787538
